checking: Work toward one well-supported solution. Keep the relevant constraints in view and examine the soundness of each inference before committing to it.
Aim for a single, carefully justified answer. Confirm that each step follows from the previous one and that the result satisfies the requirements of the task.
Pursue one line of reasoning and make it rigorous. At each step, test whether your intermediate conclusions actually hold before building on them.
Focus on producing a correct, well-checked result. Proceed methodically, scrutinize every claim you rely on, and settle on the answer only when it withstands scrutiny.
exploratory: Develop several plausible approaches. Revisit your assumptions, compare alternatives, and delay commitment until the possibilities have been considered.
Generate multiple candidate directions before choosing. Challenge your initial framing, weigh competing options against each other, and stay open to changing course.
Cast a wide net: brainstorm different angles on the task, reconsider what you took for granted, and contrast the alternatives before deciding.
Explore rather than converge early. Try out a range of ideas, switch approaches when a new one looks promising, and only narrow down after surveying the options.
